journal.label: The journal (blog)
journal.help: Off as it ships: the shop's /journal page keeps saying “Coming soon”. You can still write, review and publish articles in Website › Blog & journal; once this is on, the published ones appear on the shop in their language. Reading time is the article's words over the words a reader reads in a minute (English and Bengali separately), never less than the shortest time you set. The product block under an article shows at most the number you set (0 = none). With “review by another person” on, nobody can pass the review of an article he wrote himself. The honest line is shown with an AI author's name; leave it empty for the shop's own words.

clusters.label: Topic plan: link rules
clusters.help: Which links the articles of a cluster must carry in Website › Blog & journal › Topic plan: a supporting article to its pillar article and to the cluster's shop page, the pillar to every live article of its cluster. The plan always shows what is missing; with “refuse publishing” on (off as it ships) such an article cannot be published or scheduled until the links are in. A new topic is compared word by word with every article and topic: from the first number it is “a little alike”, from the second “very close” and it needs a second press to add.

approval.label: Topic plan: approval
approval.help: Who decides which articles get written. “The owner” (as it ships): a topic from a writer waits for your yes; you can approve a whole month's topics with one press. “By itself”: such a topic is approved at once — a very close one still waits for you while “hold very close topics” is on — and with “publish by itself” an article from an approved topic goes live as soon as its last review step passes. The Topic plan shows what was decided by itself over the days you set.

brief.label: Blog brief form
brief.help: Every article starts from a brief in Website › Blog & journal › Brief: the topic, its language, how many words and the keywords are chosen before a word is written. A new brief starts at the word count you set and may ask for between the fewest and the most words you set. With “Start writing needs a brief” on (off as it ships) a topic cannot become an article until its brief is saved. An AI draft always needs a brief.

aiDraft.label: AI first drafts from the brief
aiDraft.help: Off as it ships. When on (and AI is on for the whole shop), a saved brief in Website › Blog & journal › Brief offers “Write the first draft with AI”: the draft is written in the brief's language from the brief alone and lands on the board as an article in writing, marked as AI-assisted; a person edits it and it passes the three review steps before anyone can publish it. Until an AI provider's key is entered the practice writer serves and says so. At most the number you set in a day.
